item.title: Israeli spy chief lobbied for joint Iran strikes on US visit, sources say
item.description:
By Alexander Cornwell

JERUSALEM, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The head of Israel's Mossad spy agency, Roman Gofman, advocated for joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran during meetings with US officials last week, according to two people briefed on the visit.

Gofman met with Trump administration officials, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe, in Washington, the people said, adding that the Mossad chief briefed the officials on Israeli intelligence on Iran.

item.title: Turkish court hands new sentence and political ban to jailed Istanbul mayor, media says
item.description:
ISTANBUL, Nov 18 (Reuters) - A Turkish court on Wednesday sentenced jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu to a furthertwo years in prison for violating the election law and imposed a new political ban on him, local media reported.

• Imamoglu was one of nine defendants sentenced to two years and one month in prison in a case concerning the opposition Republican People's Party's (CHP) convention in November 2023, state broadcaster TRT Haber said

item.title: Israel army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
item.description:
The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp.

The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security.

item.title: OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks
item.description:
By William James

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Efforts to boost electrification will depend on fossil fuels, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais said on Wednesday at the COP31 talks, where host Turkey is seeking to make increased electricity use a central outcome of the conference.

Turkey has presented a target to increase electricity's share of final energy demand worldwide to 35% by 2035 from around 20% now as a way to curb climate change driven by carbon emissions.

item.title: IAEA chief says planned US-Saudi nuclear deal 'very satisfactory' on inspections
item.description:
By Francois Murphy

VIENNA, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The provisions in a planned US-Saudi nuclear deal for inspections in Saudi Arabia are "very satisfactory" even though they do not include the gold-standard Additional Protocol, the UN nuclear watchdog's chief said on Wednesday.

The proposed deal on civil nuclear cooperation, known as a 123 agreement, has yet to be approved by US lawmakers and has been criticised by nonproliferation experts for not barring Riyadh from enriching uranium or reprocessing spent reactor fuel, two potential ⁠pathways ​to a nuclear weapon.

item.title: Tunisia olive oil exports jump nearly 50 pct on bumper harvest
item.description:
Tunisia's olive oil exports rose nearly 50 percent, official figures showed on Wednesday, after a bumper harvest that made it the world's second biggest producer after Spain.

Exports jumped 47.7 percent to 413,100 tonnes during the season that ended in October, earning revenues of $1.7 billion, the National Agricultural Observatory said.

Tunisia produced more than 500,000 tonnes of olive oil this season, a five-year record. Agriculture accounts for 10 percent of the country's GDP, according to official figures.

item.title: Explainer-What is Iraq's Kataib Hezbollah militia?
item.description:
By Michael Georgy and Ahmed Rasheed

DUBAI/BAGHDAD Nov 18 (Reuters) - Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has made his riskiest move since he came to power six months ago: directly confronting the heavily armed Shi'ite militias that function as proxies of Iran.

Zaidi has told his security forces to prepare to take onKataib Hezbollah, the most powerful Iran-aligned group, which officials have accused of running a smuggling ring that siphoned off hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of state-owned oil.

item.title: Explainer-Untangling Yemen's complex civil war
item.description:
By Angus McDowall

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Yemen's Houthis have advanced in recent days against the internationally backed government, raising concerns they might launch an offensive against its temporary capital of Aden.

WHY IS THE WAR IN YEMEN IMPORTANT?

Since Yemen's long-frozen civil war reignited this summer in a spillover from the US-Iran conflict, the Tehran-aligned Houthi group has made big gains against the internationally recognised government, fired on Red Sea shipping and attacked Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Israeli military begins a new thrust in Gaza, witnesses say
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its forces were targeting Hamas infrastructure outside areas that Israel controls in the enclave.

Witnesses said some Israeli tanks rolled onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite a ceasefire that has lasted more than a year.

item.title: Saudis preparing for Yemen campaign to last well into 2027
item.description:
(Refiles with Nov 18 dateline, correcting from Nov 17)

By Timour Azhari and Humeyra Pamuk

RIYADH, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans.

item.title: With new speaker, Israel parliament moves to unravel Netanyahu legacy
item.description:
Israel's parliament met under a new speaker from the anti-Benjamin Netanyahu bloc on Wednesday, as opponents of the caretaker prime minister began a legislative offensive to roll back his divisive legacy.

In the vote for parliament speaker late on Tuesday, 66 lawmakers out of 120 voted in favour of Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu.

item.title: US Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory': IAEA
item.description:
UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme.

The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation.

"It's a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement," Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors' meeting.

Once nuclear power development gets under way in Saudi Arabia, "we will be there," he added.

item.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears, sources say
item.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied tomilitias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray region said,fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

The build-up along the border has brought the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitorsACLED and International Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray and another person close toanti-government rebels there.

item.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
item.description:
By Alexander Cornwell

JERUSALEM, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The body overseeing US President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse.

The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.

item.title: Gulf countries under fire after US hits Iran island
item.description:
Gulf nations scrambled to intercept incoming fire  from Iran and its allies on Wednesday after the US struck an Iranian island, as rising violence threatened efforts to resolve the Middle East war.

Kuwait activated its air defences to counter drone strikes -- the first since early September -- and Bahrain said it fended off an Iranian attack, after the United States struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the flashpoint Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Italy approves antisemitism law amid leftist opposition protests
item.description:
By Angelo Amante

ROME, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Italy's parliament has given final approval to a bill aimed at combating antisemitism, which includes a contentious definition critics say could limit freedom of expression and advocacy for Palestinian rights.

The legislation, which the lower house adopted late on Tuesday by 147 votes to 93, enshrines the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) definition of antisemitism, which lists some forms of criticism of Israel as examples of antisemitic conduct.

item.title: Iran fires at Kuwait after US strike on Iranian island
item.description:
By Enas Alashray and Nayera Abdallah

DUBAI, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Iran said it targeted US drone and missile sites in Kuwait overnight after the United States struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, marking Tehran's first attack on the US-allied Gulf state since September.

Underlining a broader uptick in hostilities in recent days, Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on Wednesday for a third time in a week, accusing Tehran of a "systematic hostile approach" towards the Gulf kingdom, where the US Navy's Fifth Fleet is headquartered.

item.title: Gulf nations attacked after US strikes Iranian island
item.description:
Bahrain and Kuwait said Wednesday that they had repelled air attacks launched against them following US strikes on an Iranian island, as Gulf nations face retaliatory bombardment in the Middle East war.

The conflict -- which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February -- has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities.

item.title: Pakistani man convicted of plotting to kill Trump is sentenced to over 27 years in prison
item.description:
By Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Nov 17 (Reuters) - A US judge sentenced a Pakistani man to more than 27 years in prison for plotting in 2024 to kill President Donald Trump and other prominent US politicians at the behest of Iran, the Department of Justice said on Tuesday.

"Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Asif Merchant, 48, of Pakistan, was sentenced by US District Judge Eric RKomitee to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire," the DOJ said in a statement.

item.title: Australia sanctions Israeli settlers, organisations over West Bank expansion
item.description:
By Renju Jose

SYDNEY, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Australia on Wednesday imposed sanctions on three Israeli individuals and four organisations for illegal settlement expansion and settler violence in the West Bank, saying those actions were extinguishing the possibility of a two-state solution.

Australia's move follows Britain's decision on Tuesday to sanction eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank.
